items.consigne: Read the printed word. Tell or show one letter–sound clue that helped you.
items.stimulus: Word: `map`. No picture and no spoken model.
items.reponse_attendue: Correct reading: **map** /mæp/. Graphemes `m|a|p`; acceptable clue `a` spells /æ/, or `m` /m/, or `p` /p/. Letter-name recital alone is insufficient.
criteres: Reads printed map recognizably with the target short vowel.
Shows at least one actual grapheme–phoneme link.
Does not merely name letters or guess from a picture.
items.feedback: If only letter names are supplied, contrast a letter name with its sound; ask the learner to blend, then retry on a DIFFERENT practice word.
items.representation: printed CVC + oral decoding + pointed grapheme; actual word pronunciation (or approved sequential phoneme-output) plus observed grapheme clue
items.variations_permises: Font and accessible spoken/phoneme-output modality; word unchanged.
items.limites_variation: Ne modifier ni mots imprimés, ni graphèmes ciblés, ni corrigé; pas d’image-indice, de modèle oral ni de génération IA libre. Les adaptations de lecture ne doivent pas fournir le son ou le mot.

items.consigne: Read the word. Identify the middle grapheme and its short vowel sound.
items.stimulus: Word: `bed`. A single clear printed card on a neutral background; no picture, example word, contextual hint or spoken model.
items.reponse_attendue: Correct: **bed** /bɛd/. Middle `e` spells /ɛ/. Not *bad* /bæd/; the pupil’s evidence must refer to the printed `e`.
criteres: Correct recognizable pronunciation of bed.
Accurately points to e and links it to /ɛ/.
Can demonstrate sound joining without a letter-name substitution.
items.feedback: If the response is bad, point to the grapheme actually printed in the middle and compare it with the short e sound; do not say the whole target word before a later fresh attempt.
items.representation: short-vowel evidence, single word; actual word pronunciation (or approved sequential phoneme-output) plus observed grapheme clue
items.variations_permises: Large-print e, oral/pointer cue after pronunciation only.
items.limites_variation: Ne modifier ni mots imprimés, ni graphèmes ciblés, ni corrigé; pas d’image-indice, de modèle oral ni de génération IA libre. Les adaptations de lecture ne doivent pas fournir le son ou le mot.

items.consigne: Read this word by sound blending. Show how many graphemes it contains and explain the final one.
items.stimulus: Word: `cash`. Analyse with letter tiles after initial read.
items.reponse_attendue: Correct **cash** /kæʃ/; `c|a|sh` are three graphemes; `sh` (two letters) represents the single phoneme /ʃ/. Four letters do not imply four phonemes.
criteres: Reads cash with the final /ʃ/ sound.
Segments into three graphèmes c|a|sh.
Correctly links sh to /ʃ/.
items.feedback: If the learner separates s and h, place them in one tile as a remedial hint only after the attempt, and have them read another word.
items.representation: word print and 3 phoneme boxes; actual word pronunciation (or approved sequential phoneme-output) plus observed grapheme clue
items.variations_permises: Only size/placement of tiles may vary; do not supply sh pronunciation.
items.limites_variation: Ne modifier ni mots imprimés, ni graphèmes ciblés, ni corrigé; pas d’image-indice, de modèle oral ni de génération IA libre. Les adaptations de lecture ne doivent pas fournir le son ou le mot.

items.consigne: Read the word and identify the two-letter grapheme giving its first speech sound.
items.stimulus: Word: `chin`. No picture or actor demonstration.
criteres: Reads chin recognizably with /tʃ/.
Points to ch as a two-letter grapheme.
States or demonstrates one /tʃ/ sound for ch.
items.feedback: If the pupil says /k/ at the start, contrast ch with a single c on a practice strip after the attempt, then recheck a new ch word.

items.consigne: Read both words, compare the middle grapheme and say why the words differ.
items.stimulus: Printed pair: `sit` / `set`, mixed order, no context picture.
items.reponse_attendue: Correct **sit** /sɪt/ (`i` → /ɪ/) versus **set** /sɛt/ (`e` → /ɛ/). Both have s and t, but different short middle vowel graphèmes. Do not use letter names alone.
criteres: Both words decoded correctly.
Identifies the changed grapheme i/e.
Links each vowel with its sound in these words.
items.feedback: If the learner pronounces both alike, isolate i and e and review each correspondence with separate words before comparing again.
items.representation: minimal pair CVC + vowel comparison; actual word pronunciation (or approved sequential phoneme-output) plus observed grapheme clue
items.variations_permises: Presentation order can vary, but both spellings and vowel mappings fixed.

items.consigne: Read the word, then explain whether the first two letters represent one speech sound or two.
items.stimulus: Word: `slip` on a card. Optional blank boxes for sounds after reading.
items.reponse_attendue: Correct **slip** /slɪp/; `s` /s/ and `l` /l/ are two phonemes, so `sl` is a consonant blend, unlike `sh` /ʃ/ as a digraph. `i` spells short /ɪ/.
criteres: Reads slip recognizably with /s/ and /l/.
Explains or shows s and l as two separate sounds.
Distinguishes a consonant cluster from the one-sound sh digraph.
items.feedback: If sl is mistakenly treated as /ʃ/, let the learner feel two sequential speech sounds; compare one letter tile per sound after the first attempt.
items.representation: consonant cluster compared with digraph; actual word pronunciation (or approved sequential phoneme-output) plus observed grapheme clue

items.consigne: Read both labels without an image. Give a vowel clue in the first and a digraph clue in the second.
items.reponse_attendue: Correct **pet** /pɛt/, middle `e` = /ɛ/; **fish** /fɪʃ/, ending `sh` = /ʃ/; fish has 3 graphemes f|i|sh and 3 phonemes.
criteres: Both words decoded from print.
Gives e→/ɛ/ for pet.
Gives sh→/ʃ/ for fish.
No inference from illustration.
items.feedback: If fish is said with two sounds for sh, box the digraph AFTER the first attempt and have the student retry with a different practice word.

items.reponse_attendue: Correct **mud** /mʌd/ with u→/ʌ/; **chat** /tʃæt/ with ch→/tʃ/ (or a→/æ/), joined left-to-right. The scene label provides context, not a word hint.

items.consigne: Independent proof A — Discovery journal. Read each NEW printed label aloud in English (or by pre-approved phoneme-output modality), then point to a grapheme and state its sound for EACH word. Work without adult hints. You may take an independent moment to sound out a word.
items.stimulus: Four picture-free labels in a fictional discovery journal: `hen`, `pin`, `rug`, `shed`. All four spellings are held out from demonstrations and practice; sh must be treated as a digraph.
items.reponse_attendue:
Context A — discovery journal: four independently decoded English print labels, with documented grapheme–sound evidence.
`hen` = /h/ /ɛ/ /n/ → **hen**; units `h | e | n`; expected clue `e` spells /ɛ/. Other correct single-grapheme sound links are acceptable if accurately shown.
`pin` = /p/ /ɪ/ /n/ → **pin**; units `p | i | n`; expected clue `i` spells /ɪ/. Other correct single-grapheme sound links are acceptable if accurately shown.
`rug` = /r/ /ʌ/ /g/ → **rug**; units `r | u | g`; expected clue `u` spells /ʌ/. Other correct single-grapheme sound links are acceptable if accurately shown.
`shed` = /ʃ/ /ɛ/ /d/ → **shed**; units `sh | e | d`; expected clue `sh` spells /ʃ/. Other correct single-grapheme sound links are acceptable if accurately shown.
Teacher accepts English pronunciation variants preserving taught contrasts. Pupil may self-correct without a cue. A picture, memory, automatic word-reader or adult prompt does not count as independent code evidence.
criteres: M1 — At least 3 of the 4 new printed words are decoded recognizably using sound–grapheme correspondences, without word prompts.
M2 — At least 3 of the 4 words have a specific correct grapheme–phoneme clue pointed out, said or produced with approved access tools.
M3 — The target digraph (sh in A, ch in B) is read with its one correct consonant sound AND is justified by the two-letter grapheme.
M4 — Blending from left to right is observed for new words; letter names alone or contextual guessing are not accepted.
M5 — All four words are attempted autonomously; no adult model, external word-reader or corrective code cue during the proof.
items.feedback: If a short vowel is wrong, practise that vowel on other regular words; if shed is read without the sh sound, retrain a digraph in one box. Schedule a later unseen assessment, not a coached redo scored as first attempt.
items.representation: four new English word labels, audible decoding or equivalent phoneme-output, one grounded printed clue per label; actual word pronunciation (or approved sequential phoneme-output) plus observed grapheme clue
items.variations_permises: Only typography, reading time, access device, and order of label presentation may vary without changing spellings. No pictures or verbal cues may predict the answer.
items.limites_variation: Ne modifier ni mots imprimés, ni graphèmes ciblés, ni corrigé; pas d’image-indice, de modèle oral ni de génération IA libre. Les adaptations de lecture ne doivent pas fournir le son ou le mot.

items.consigne: Independent proof B — Makers’ workshop. Read each NEW printed equipment label (no pictures) from English spelling, then identify one grapheme and its sound for EACH label. No model or answer-revealing aid; do not reuse journal labels.
items.stimulus: Four picture-free labels in a fictional workshop: `web`, `fin`, `mug`, `chip`. Each is unseen during teaching and distinct from proof A; ch is a digraph.
items.reponse_attendue:
Context B — makers’ workshop: four independently decoded English print labels, with documented grapheme–sound evidence.
`web` = /w/ /ɛ/ /b/ → **web**; units `w | e | b`; expected clue `e` spells /ɛ/. Other correct single-grapheme sound links are acceptable if accurately shown.
`fin` = /f/ /ɪ/ /n/ → **fin**; units `f | i | n`; expected clue `i` spells /ɪ/. Other correct single-grapheme sound links are acceptable if accurately shown.
`mug` = /m/ /ʌ/ /g/ → **mug**; units `m | u | g`; expected clue `u` spells /ʌ/. Other correct single-grapheme sound links are acceptable if accurately shown.
`chip` = /tʃ/ /ɪ/ /p/ → **chip**; units `ch | i | p`; expected clue `ch` spells /tʃ/. Other correct single-grapheme sound links are acceptable if accurately shown.
Teacher accepts English pronunciation variants preserving taught contrasts. Pupil may self-correct without a cue. A picture, memory, automatic word-reader or adult prompt does not count as independent code evidence.
criteres: M1 — At least 3 of the 4 new printed words are decoded recognizably using sound–grapheme correspondences, without word prompts.
M2 — At least 3 of the 4 words have a specific correct grapheme–phoneme clue pointed out, said or produced with approved access tools.
M3 — The target digraph (sh in A, ch in B) is read with its one correct consonant sound AND is justified by the two-letter grapheme.
M4 — Blending from left to right is observed for new words; letter names alone or contextual guessing are not accepted.
M5 — All four words are attempted autonomously; no adult model, external word-reader or corrective code cue during the proof.
items.feedback: If chip begins with /k/ rather than /tʃ/, practise the ch digraph on other novel practice cards and reassess in a third context. If an accent issue is suspected, verify printed clue before classifying a decoding error.
